added_edges.relationship: First published in 1972 to develop feminist scholarship in conversation with the women’s movement, including historical research and early Berkshire Conference issues.
added_edges.evidence_note: An interdisciplinary women’s-studies institution with a documented women’s-history component. The edge does not restrict its programme to history or date the origin of women’s history to 1972; organizing began in 1969.

added_edges.relationship: Launched in 1975 to provide an interdisciplinary forum for the expanding scholarship on women, including historical inquiry and documentary recovery.
added_edges.evidence_note: Links the historical component of a broader feminist scholarly programme. This is neither a claim of exclusive disciplinary affiliation nor an origin date for all women’s history.

added_edges.relationship: Launched in 1976 as an institutional forum for historical explanation drawing selectively on social-science theories and methods.
added_edges.evidence_note: An institutional project within the broad social-history expansion, with qualitative as well as quantitative methods. Its interdisciplinary scope exceeds this atlas entry; it does not endorse every approach listed in the entry.

added_edges.relationship: Launched in 1927 to develop economic and social historical inquiry, articulated in the first issue through Ashley’s programme and the journal’s original subtitle.
added_edges.evidence_note: Consolidates an existing field through a society journal. The programme included social history and cannot be reduced to later cliometrics; 1926 is the society’s foundation, not this first publication date.

added_edges.relationship: Launched in 1973 as an annual forum combining Oral History Association colloquium papers and contributed articles for the developing practice of oral history.
added_edges.evidence_note: One institutional forum in a much older and internationally diverse practice. The US association, its newsletter and the separate British journal Oral History are not conflated.

added_edges.relationship: Founded in 1974 as a methodological forum for African history, emphasizing critical scrutiny of historical sources and the ways historians use them.
added_edges.evidence_note: A specific source-critical programme within African historiography, not the creation of African historical thought or an assignment of every African historian to one method. Claim limited to the available first-editorial extract.

added_edges.relationship: Launched in 1989 to make gender’s historical experience and significance a focused programme of historical inquiry.
added_edges.evidence_note: Retrospective abstract-level evidence supports this limited founding-purpose claim. The target is the gender-history component of the combined Gender & racial formation entry; the edge does not date or subsume every racial-formation approach.

added_edges.relationship: Launched in 1970 to develop interdisciplinary historical methods, giving quantitative analysis a place within a wider exchange with the social sciences and other disciplines.
added_edges.evidence_note: The quantitative connection is one explicit component of a broader founding programme. The journal is not exclusively quantitative and the link does not equate its programme with all cliometric or serial-history approaches.

added_edges.relationship: Established as a project in 1912 to institutionalize history of science through Sarton’s programme of historical synthesis, set out in the first volume published in 1913.
added_edges.evidence_note: Preserves the existing 1912 foundation date and explicitly distinguishes 1913 first publication. The initial Sartonian synthesis is one programme within history of science; it does not characterize the entire field or the journal’s later pluralism.

added_edges.relationship: Launched in 1958 to create a forum for comparative inquiry across history and the social sciences, bringing specialists into discussion of recurring historical problems.
added_edges.evidence_note: Its comparative programme offers an institutional home for historical sociology but extends to anthropology and the humanities. The edge neither reduces the journal to sociology nor assigns it the later state-formation theories in this atlas entry.

added_edges.relationship: Launched in 1995 to broaden environmental history’s geographical and disciplinary conversation, including work on Africa, Asia and other regions alongside Europe and North America.
added_edges.evidence_note: An expansion and consolidation project in an already established field. Its explicit geographical ambitions provide evidence against treating North American environmental-history venues as the field’s whole institutional history.

added_edges.relationship: Launched in 1995 to consolidate interdisciplinary research and scholarly exchange on nations and nationalism through an association journal.
added_edges.evidence_note: A field-consolidating institution after earlier decades of nationalism scholarship, not the field’s beginning or an endorsement of a single explanation of nations.

added_edges.relationship: Launched in 1986 to provide an interdisciplinary forum for Holocaust research in conversation with the wider scholarly study of genocide.
added_edges.evidence_note: The edge connects the Holocaust component of a wider programme to the existing atlas entry. Comparative genocide studies is not thereby claimed to be comprehensively represented by that entry; the evidence is contemporary reception, not a full reading of the founding editorial.

added_edges.relationship: Launched in 1984 to bring historians and anthropologists into a shared forum where each discipline could reconsider its methods through the other’s work.
added_edges.evidence_note: A particular institutional exchange, not the origin of historical anthropology. Distinct from Stocking’s History of Anthropology series, which the same contemporary review contrasts with this journal; intended collaboration does not prove that disciplinary divisions disappeared.

journal_b37c47d6d6bf8912.note: First publication in 1973 documented by the contemporary OHA launch notice. The included 1972 colloquium is not the publication start. Cessation and present continuity remain unverified.

journal_55b2862e091c93c6.note: First volume and founding editorial published in 1974. Existing library format/end observations remain attributed evidence; no cessation or present continuity is inferred.

changed_journals.label: Comparative Studies in Society and History
Signs: Journal of Women in Culture and Society

limitations: Targeted programme review, not a completed worldwide journal census.
Journal foundation/consolidation is not the date of origin of a whole field.
Gap findings are editorial assessments, not automatic new atlas entries.
